title: Two things come back: summary and blob
text: And hands you back two things: a readable summary and an opaque encrypted blob. The natural guess is that the summary, the part you can read, is what carries the memory forward. Pass it alone into the next call and the context breaks anyway. Here's the concrete case.

title: The anchor: a twenty-turn conversation
text: A 20-turn conversation overflows and compaction fires. You get back content, earlier conversation summarized in plain English right next to encrypted content, a sealed string starting epobcioidxgc. Thread the readable text into the next call and context breaks. Thread the blob back instead and it holds. Here's why.

title: Why: display text vs. server-verifiable token
text: The readable text is display in debug only. It's for you, not for the model. The encrypted blob is a server-verifiable token. It reconstructs the full compressed context, turn boundaries, roles, metadata, everything the plain summary throws away.

title: The anchor returns: one token, not a replay
text: So, on the next call, you pass only the blob. The server doesn't replay 20 messages. It rebuilds the full context straight from the token. Passing the blob restores everything compaction saved.
